title: Autonomous Revert Controller with Confidence Scoring and State Harmonizer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an Autonomous Revert Controller (ARC) that detects unsafe configuration changes affecting cost or reliability and automatically reverts them when confidence thresholds are met. ARC combines multiple signals (latency p95 deviation, per-token cost variance, KV cache miss rate, and evaluation-set quality regressions) into a confidence score that drives a staged revert pipeline. The system must be conservative by default (high hysteresis, staged canaries, simulated dry-run) and auditable (change snapshots, event logs, and human-in-the-loop approval hooks).
acceptance_criteria: ARC computes a single confidence score from configured signals and emits an actionable revert decision when score >= threshold
Configuration apply workflow supports dry-run and simulated traffic to predict cost/latency deltas before commit
Automatic revert path can revert a config change within 3 minutes of trigger for hosted API and 10 minutes for Dedicated pools, with safe state reconciliation and no duplicate rollbacks
Revert actions are idempotent and produce a detailed audit record (snapshot before, patch applied, snapshot after, reason, confidence breakdown)
Operators can override automatic reverts via a 5-minute human confirmation window for critical changes
All revert events surface to Console with per-route breadcrumbs, cost delta chart, and linked PR/Confluence artifacts
implementation_notes: Signals to include: latency_p95_delta, per_token_cost_zscore, kv_cache_miss_rate, model_quality_regression (from eval harness), error_rate_spike
Normalize signals to a 0-1 range and weight via config; initial weights: latency 0.35, cost 0.30, quality 0.25, kv-cache 0.05, errors 0.05
Confidence scoring uses a sigmoid aggregation + hysteresis window (default 10m) to avoid flapping

On trigger, create a transactional revert plan: mark change as reverting (state 'reverting'), attempt atomic apply of previous config, verify health checks pass (smoke tests + sampling of live traffic), and finalize revert with audit event
Maintain an event-sourced timeline for each config change (apply,dry-run,canary,rolled-back,finalized) stored in change-log partitioned by customer and route
Use optimistic concurrency: if a newer config was applied since the triggering change, ARC enters reconcile mode and opens a ticket rather than forcibly reverting
Support simulation mode that replays sampled QPS against candidate config in a sandboxed path to predict cost/latency impact (budgeted local worker pool)
Integrate with existing rollout controller to pause/stop canaries and trigger ARC decision path
Expose feature flags to reduce aggressiveness per-customer (aggressive|balanced|conservative) and per-route thresholds
Design for multi-cluster: revert action must route to the cluster where change originated and fallback to last-known-good global policy if cluster unreachable
test_plan: Unit tests for signal normalization and confidence math (edge cases: NaN, extreme outliers)
Integration tests: simulate a config that increases batching sizes and KV cache TTL resulting in cost spike, verify ARC triggers and reverts in lab
Chaos test: mid-apply concurrent config change should put ARC into reconcile mode and produce a non-destructive alert
E2E smoke: apply change to a canary pool, induce latency regression, ensure revert path completes and metrics return to baseline
Load test: ensure ARC handles 500 concurrent config-change events without duplicate revert operations
Security review: validate ARC cannot be used to escalate privileges or revert RBAC-sensitive configs without approval
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit + integration tests, local simulation harness (this ticket)
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable ARC in dry-run mode for 10% of internal config changes, log decisions but do not revert
Phase 2 (staged auto): enable ARC auto-revert for internal non-critical routes with conservative thresholds and 5-minute human-wait window
Phase 3 (customer opt-in): provide Console toggle for tenants to opt into ARC aggressive or conservative modes
Phase 4 (wider): default to conservative auto-revert for platform-managed routes after 4 weeks of stable metrics and postmortem review
Rollback of ARC itself: feature-flagged revert disable switch and circuit-breaker that stops ARC if it exceeds 1 revert/minute or triggers >5 false positives in 24h
monitoring_playbook: Alert: ARC_revert_executed (level: P1) — includes change_key, confidence_score, signal_breakdown, timestamps
Alert: ARC_revert_failed (level: P0) — immediate paging and automatic mitigation to quarantine the route
Dashboards: per-customer revert rate, time-to-revert histogram, distribution of confidence scores, false-positive ratio vs human interventions
SLOs: revert success rate >= 99% within configured target window; false positive rate < 0.5% for production routes
Runbook: steps to investigate revert (view change timeline, replay simulation, check canary traffic slices, escalate to on-call runtime engineer)
Postmortem guideline: within 72h for any revert that causes customer-visible disruption; mandatory cross-team review if revert was suppressed by human override
